goal: A pull request stacked on another one passes ledger-verify when its ledgers are honest, instead of failing because the merge commit's first parent isn't on main.
changed: ci/pr_base.py picks a pull request's base. It is the merge commit's first parent, as before, or when that isn't on origin/<base> (a GitHub stack: github.base_ref names main while refs/pull/<n>/merge sits on the parent branch), their merge base: the newest commit of origin/<base> the pull request contains. A parent with no history in common with origin/<base> still fails.
action.yml calls it instead of failing the stacked case. The S3 spec's Base rule and the base input's description say the same.

claims.claim: A stacked pull request with honest ledgers passes, checked against the main commit the stack forked from, with a notice saying so.
claims.check: cd tests && python3.12 -m unittest test_scan.ActionScriptTest (test_a_stacked_pull_request_is_checked_against_the_main_commit_it_forked_from), which runs the Action's real step on a git repo built like a GitHub stack
claims.remaining: Seen in a real stack only as the failure (lyddonb/curator#273 and #274, 2026-11-24); the pass on GitHub follows once a project pins this commit.

claims.claim: A stack whose lower pull request rewrites a merged line on main still fails with base-changed, and a first parent with no history in common with main is refused.
The three new tests fail with origin/main's action.yml, and the whole suite passes with this one.
claims.check: the same ActionScriptTest run with origin/main's action.yml: 3 failures; then python3.12 -m unittest discover -s tests

next.item: Tag a release and bump curator's pin (.github/workflows/ledger.yml, lyddonb/agent-ledger@f77709d) to it
next.why_now: curator merges stacked pull requests now (P11 B1 was a stack of three), and each one above the bottom failed ledger-verify until the one below it merged.
next.impact: Beau stops seeing a red ledger-verify on every stacked curator pull request, so a red check there means a real ledger problem again.

release.note: ledger-verify no longer fails a pull request stacked on another one: it checks the stack against the newest base-branch commit it contains.
